meta.title: RegBench
meta.subtitle: Picking regulators from JLCPCB shelf stock made simpler

variants.name: LM317
variants.topology: Linear · positive adj.
notes: LM338 / LM350 use the same equation — swap in for more current.
Keep R1 close to the part so the 1.25 V reference is sensed at the regulator.

supportComponents.note: tantalum; add protection diodes above 25 V out

variants.name: LM337
variants.topology: Linear · negative adj.
notes: Negative rail twin of the LM317; magnitudes below, output is −Vout.

variants.name: AMS1117-ADJ / LM1117-ADJ
variants.topology: Linear · LDO adj.
notes: Fixed versions are Basic parts: AMS1117-3.3 (C6186), AMS1117-5.0 (C6187) — skip the divider if one fits.
Wants some output ESR for stability — tantalum out is the safe choice.

skus.manufacturer: Jiangsu Changjing Electronics Technology Co Ltd
Jiangsu Changjing Electronics Technology Co Ltd

variants.name: XL1509-ADJ
variants.topology: Buck · 150 kHz · 2 A
notes: LM2596-style clone that is still a Basic part. Fixed 5 V version: XL1509-5.0 (C61063).

supportComponents.note: 2× in parallel; low-ESR electrolytic also fine

variants.name: LM2596S-ADJ
variants.topology: Buck · 150 kHz · 3 A
variants.packageNote: TO-263-5 (code = UMW clone; TI/ON via search)
notes: Fixed 5 V version is Basic: LM2596SX-5.0 (C10002).
Datasheet wants a low-ESR electrolytic on the output (~220 µF) — electrolytics are Extended parts at JLCPCB.

variants.name: LM2576-ADJ
variants.topology: Buck · 52 kHz · 3 A
notes: Slow sibling of the LM2596 — bigger inductor, cheaper everything else. Fixed 5 V is Basic: LM2576SX-5.0 (C34465).

variants.name: TPS54331
variants.topology: Buck · 570 kHz · 3 A
notes: Non-synchronous — needs the catch diode.
Compensation network (R3/C6/C7 on COMP) comes from the datasheet's design procedure; the 470 pF/100 pF below cover the common 3.3–5 V designs.

variants.name: TPS5430
variants.topology: Buck · 500 kHz · 3 A
notes: Internally compensated — genuinely easy to lay out. Needs the catch diode.

variants.name: MP1584
variants.topology: Buck · 100k–1.5 MHz · 3 A · NRND
notes: ⚠ NRND — MPS marks the MP1584 "not recommended for new designs; refer to MP2338". Fine for hobby boards, but pick the MP2338 for anything long-lived.
The chip on every purple eBay module. Was a Basic part, now Extended — still cheap.
Frequency-set resistor (FREQ pin) and feed-forward cap across R-top per datasheet.

variants.name: MP2338
variants.topology: Buck · sync · COT 450 kHz · 3 A
variants.bottomResistorHint: Table 1 uses 9.09–51 k; keep 5–30 µA through R2
notes: MPS's designated successor to the MP1584 — synchronous (no diode), ±1.5% ref over temperature, 10 nA FB bias.
Feed-forward cap across R1 per datasheet Table 1 (82–470 pF by Vout); optional 10 k RT in series with FB for compensation.
Datasheet BOM: 2× 10 µF + 0.1 µF in, 2× 22 µF out, 22 nF soft-start, 0.1 µF BST.

supportComponents.note: across R1 — 82 pF at 1/12 V, 300–470 pF mid-range

variants.name: TPS54560B
variants.topology: Buck · 5 A · 60 V-in
notes: The high-current, high-voltage option in the compare set — 60 V input and 5 A out.
Non-synchronous: needs a catch diode rated well above your Vin (SS54 tops out at 40 V — use a 100 V Schottky for 48 V rails). External compensation on COMP.

supportComponents.note: SS54 C22452 only to 40 V-in; search higher
plus series R-C per datasheet procedure

variants.name: TPS54202
variants.topology: Buck · sync · 500 kHz · 2 A
notes: Cheap TI synchronous buck in SOT-23-6 — 28 V input tolerance for 24 V rails. Verify your grade's Vref tolerance in the datasheet.

variants.name: XL4015
variants.topology: Buck · 180 kHz · 5 A
variants.bottomResistorHint: the CC/CV modules hang a 10 k pot here
notes: The chip on the CC/CV "lab supply" modules. 5 A with a big inductor and real copper — budget for heat.
Needs a ≥5 A Schottky catch diode.

supportComponents.note: SS54 is 5 A — parallel or search bigger

variants.name: XL7015
variants.topology: Buck · 150 kHz · 0.8 A · 80 V-in
variants.bottomResistorHint: keep the bottom leg a few k
variants.limits: Vin 5–80 V · 0.8 A (derate to ~0.6 A at 48→5 V) · Vout ≤ 20 V
notes: The 80 V-input oddball — e-bike packs, 48 V telecom, solar strings. Modest current; derate hard at big step-downs.
Catch diode must be rated above Vin — 100 V Schottky for 48–80 V rails.

supportComponents.note: search 100 V, e.g. SS110/B5819W only to 40 V

variants.name: SY8089A
variants.topology: Buck · sync · ~1 MHz · 2 A
notes: Single-cell / 5 V-rail specialist: 2 A from a SOT-23-5 with a tiny inductor. fsw and Vref tolerance are ballpark — confirm against the Silergy datasheet before finalizing.

variants.name: SY8113B
variants.topology: Buck · sync · 3 A
notes: 3 A from a TSOT-23-6, everywhere in cheap dev boards. fsw and Vref tolerance are ballpark — confirm against the Silergy datasheet (SY8113I variant: C479075).

variants.name: MP2315
variants.topology: Buck · sync · 500 kHz · 3 A
variants.bottomResistorHint: datasheet uses ~40 k top / 13 k bottom class
notes: Synchronous — no external diode. Check MP2315S vs MP2315 pinout before copying a layout.

variants.name: MP2307
variants.topology: Buck · sync · 340 kHz · 3 A
notes: The Mini-360 module chip. Synchronous, no diode needed.

variants.name: MP1482
variants.topology: Buck · 340 kHz · 2 A
notes: Was a Basic part, now Extended — verified LCSC code.

variants.name: MP2451
variants.topology: Buck · 0.6 A · 36 V-in
notes: Handy for always-on housekeeping rails from 24 V systems.

variants.name: MP2359
variants.topology: Buck · 1.4 MHz · 1.2 A
notes: Fast switcher → tiny inductor. Needs the catch diode (B5819W is fine at 1.2 A).

variants.name: TPS562208
variants.topology: Buck · sync · D-CAP2 · 580 kHz · 2 A
notes: D-CAP2 control — keep the divider impedance in the datasheet's range and use ceramic output caps. FCCM (always-PWM); TPS562201 is the pulse-skip sibling.

variants.name: MC34063
variants.topology: Buck / boost / invert · ≤100 kHz
notes: Through-hole builds: MC34063ECN DIP-8 is C5180; AZ34063UMTR (Diodes, SOIC) is C99659 — both Extended.
The 1980s survivor. Timing cap sets frequency; sense resistor sets current limit (basics only stock 100 mΩ 1206 — C25334 — parallel/series to taste).

variants.name: MT3608
variants.topology: Boost · 1.2 MHz · 2 A switch
variants.bottomResistorHint: the blue modules use ~7.5 k + pot
variants.limits: Vin 2–24 V · Vout ≤ 28 V · 2 A switch (Iout = Isw × Vin/Vout − margin)
notes: The chip on every blue boost module. Output current is switch-limited: at 5→12 V expect ≲0.7 A.
Needs the Schottky to the output (SS34-class) — boost topology, so remember Vout appears at the input when idle.

variants.name: TPS62000 (adj)
variants.topology: Buck · sync · 750 kHz · 0.6 A
variants.bottomResistorHint: keep R1+R2 ≤ 1 MΩ; datasheet example uses 180 k bottom
variants.limits: Vin 2–5.5 V · 0.6 A (0.2 A below 2.5 V-in) · Vout 0.8–VIN
notes: Battery-rail buck from the example datasheet: 1–3 cell input, 100% duty for dropout, ILIM pin sets 0.6/1.2 A switch limit.
Stability wants a feed-forward cap across R1: C-ff ≈ 1/(2π·30k·R1) below 1 µF-out designs — see datasheet Eq. 2–3. Total accuracy spec is ±3–4%, so the ±2% ref default here is a guess.

variants.name: TPS61040
variants.topology: Boost · 1 MHz · 400 mA sw
variants.bottomResistorHint: high-Z divider preserves the low Iq
notes: Classic LCD-bias / small-boost part. Add ~10 pF feed-forward across R1.

variants.name: TL431 / CJ431
variants.topology: Shunt reference
notes: Shunt topology: needs a bias resistor from the supply sized so cathode current stays in 1–100 mA over load.

supportComponents.description: (Vsupply − Vout) / ~5 mA — pick from the resistor table

supportComponents.note: check the TL431 stability region for large caps
